passage: In the small-town house Salma crouched at the far end of the sofa while Vaibhav counted. Salma thought: "If he goes left, I go right around the sofa. If he goes right, I go left." Vaibhav stopped counting and turned, and Salma watched his feet, holding still. He stepped left. Salma slid quietly around the right end and behind the curtain, heart thumping, biting back a grin.

qa.q: What was Salma feeling while watching Vaibhav's feet?
qa.a: Salma was tense and excited, shown by the thumping heart and the grin held back.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Salma use if Vaibhav guesses the plan, and why?
qa.a: Salma could pick a hiding place that is out of sight of both ends of the sofa, because a plan that depends on which way the seeker goes fails if he reads it.

qa.q: How does Vaibhav see the game when Salma vanishes?
qa.a: Vaibhav, who went left, is likely puzzled and may guess at the other end, since he has no idea Salma is following his moves.

grounding: A child thinks that if the seeker goes left, the child goes right around the sofa, a simple plan about another person's move.

passage: Behind the sofa in the Oslo flat, Emil crouched and listened. Tuan was counting by the window. "Eight, nine, ten! Coming!" Emil peeked round the side. If Tuan walks left, I'll go right, he thought. Tuan's socks padded left. Emil slid right, around the far arm of the sofa, and stayed low. Tuan looked behind the sofa, found nothing and scratched his head.

qa.a: Tuan was counting by the window.

qa.q: What was Emil thinking as he peeked round the side?
qa.a: He was alert and a little nervous, planning to go right if Tuan went left.

qa.q: What would you change in Emil's plan if Tuan turned back?
qa.a: He could watch again and move the other way, since his rule depends on Tuan's move.

qa.q: How does the sofa look to Tuan?
qa.a: Tuan is puzzled, because he checks behind it and finds nothing.

grounding: A child makes a simple if-then plan about which way the seeker goes around the sofa and moves the other way.

passage: At the community centre's rainy-day play hour, Siddharth crouched behind the long sofa in the reading corner. Zubin was seeking. Siddharth held his breath and whispered to himself, "If he goes by the shelves, I go by the window." Zubin's trainers squeaked toward the shelves. Siddharth crawled the other way, around the far end. Zubin reached the spot where Siddharth had been and found only a cushion.

qa.q: What did Zubin find behind the sofa?
What was Siddharth feeling as Zubin's trainers squeaked closer?
qa.a: He was probably tense and excited, ready to move the other way.

qa.q: What else could Siddharth do if Zubin comes round both ends?
qa.a: He could pick a new hiding place altogether, since his rule only works if Zubin chooses one side.

qa.q: If you were Zubin, what would you think?
qa.a: You would feel puzzled that the spot was empty, and might start guessing that Siddharth is moving around.

grounding: A child plans "if the seeker goes one way, I go the other" around a sofa and uses it to stay hidden.
